note: Most studio tracks are by Zarsanga, the voice most identified with tappa; the Afghan field recordings (1966 to 1970) show the same songs in village and teahouse settings. Romanised Pashto titles have no single standard and are kept as printed on each release.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Discogs returns 136 hits for 'pashto' and 171 for 'pushto', most of them Pashto film-song 7-inch singles, a handful of Zarsanga and Gulnar Begum folk records, and Afghan field-recording LPs (Lyrichord 1971, Folkways 1977, Argo 1972, Traditional Crossroads 2003). The bulk of the genre sits on uncatalogued Peshawar cassettes (Odeon, Mehran and others from the early 1970s to about 2012), Radio Pakistan Peshawar and Radio Kabul tapes and Lok Virsa releases, so the true count is guessed from a cassette industry of many hundreds of singers each with dozens of tapes, of which a fraction is folk (tappa, charbeta, loba) rather than ghazal or film song. An insider's essential list would be about 40 performances (Zarsanga, Gulnar Begum, Kishwar Sultan, Mashooq Sultan, Hidayatullah, Khan Tehsil and classic tappa/charbeta singers).
